option_relations.rationale: Multiple hereditary infundibulocystic basal cell carcinoma syndrome (MHIBCC) is a distinct entity from Nevoid basal cell carcinoma syndrome, though both involve basal cell carcinomas. The genetic findings (SUFU mutation) are not typical for MHIBCC.
Infundibulocystic basal cell carcinoma describes a histological subtype of basal cell carcinoma, not a syndrome. The patient presents with a syndrome involving multiple lesions and systemic findings.

Basal cell nevus syndrome (Gorlin syndrome) is an alternative name for Nevoid basal cell carcinoma syndrome. The clinical presentation (multiple basal cell carcinomas, meningioma, family history) and genetic findings (SUFU mutation) are consistent with this diagnosis.

Gorlin Syndrome (Basal Cell Nevus Syndrome) is an alternative name for Nevoid basal cell carcinoma syndrome. The clinical presentation (multiple basal cell carcinomas, meningioma, family history) and genetic findings (SUFU mutation) are consistent with this diagnosis.
